subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this exact head’s custom cooperative glob walker and bootstrap scheduling as the bounded fix after comparable runtime proof, or require a narrower glob implementation?
rationale: Bootstrap file selection feeds prompt and session state, and replacing Node glob creates upgrade semantics that automation cannot approve without owner intent and final-head proof.

options.title: Require proof, then land
options.body: Request same-host current-main versus exact-head embedded-run timing, liveness, loaded-file parity, and peak RSS, then land if the results support the bounded fix.

options.title: Require a narrower glob path
options.body: Keep async reads and hook yielding but replace the custom glob engine with an off-thread or maintained contract-compatible implementation.

options.title: Pause the branch
options.body: Hold or close the PR if maintainers do not want to own custom glob semantics on a session-context path.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then land
recommendation.body: Request same-host current-main versus exact-head embedded-run timing, liveness, loaded-file parity, and peak RSS, then land if the results support the bounded fix.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest merged history across the hook, bootstrap, and workspace-read boundaries defining the tradeoff.
